record.paper_title: Open problems in nuclear structure near drip lines
record.original_question: How can time-dependent many-body theory be extended to describe weakly bound nuclei and nuclear reactions in the continuum with the correct asymptotic behavior and pairing dynamics? The unresolved tasks include solving time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov equations for pair-correlated systems in medium-mass and heavy drip-line nuclei, handling reactions with more than three particles, and resolving the conceptual problem of how to compute exclusive cross sections within time-dependent density functional theory without unphysical cross-channel correlations of the kind known from time-dependent Hartree-Fock.

evidence.quote: Firstly, we need to include the pair correlation in the density-functional approaches, which is essential for description of weakly-bound nuclei in medium- and heavy-mass regions. In other words, we should solve the time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov (TDHFB) equations which can describe the dynamics of the pair correlated many-body systems on the basis of the pairing functional Epair[ρn,ρ p, ˜ρn, ˜ρp].
However, calculation of the exclusive cross sections have some conceptual open problems we need to solve. This is similar to the famous problem of spurious cross channel correlations in TDHF [40].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop an extension of time-dependent nuclear many-body theory capable of describing weakly bound nuclei and low-energy nuclear reactions in which the asymptotic continuum and pairing correlations are simultaneously treated correctly. Concretely, address the following:

(a) Formulate and numerically solve the time-dependent Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov (TDHFB) equations for self-consistent pair-correlated many-body dynamics, based on an energy density functional E[ρ_n, ρ_p, ρ̃_n, ρ̃_p] depending on normal densities ρ_q and pairing (anomalous) densities ρ̃_q for neutrons (q=n) and protons (q=p), in medium-mass and heavy nuclei near the neutron and proton drip lines, with boundary conditions that yield correct asymptotic behavior of the quasiparticle wave functions in the continuum.

(b) Extend the formalism to nuclear reactions involving more than three interacting nucleons (or composite fragments) in the continuum, including breakup, transfer, and fusion channels.

(c) Resolve the conceptual problem of computing exclusive (channel-resolved) reaction cross sections within time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) without introducing the spurious cross-channel correlations that are known to affect time-dependent Hartree–Fock (TDHF): namely, devise a prescription that projects the time-evolved one-body (or generalized) density onto definite asymptotic reaction channels and yields physically meaningful exclusive cross sections rather than artifacts arising from the single-Slater-determinant (or single quasiparticle vacuum) ansatz.
artifact.status_search_result: TDHFB has been implemented in 3D for medium-mass and some heavy nuclei since the 2010s, partially addressing item (a). Reactions with more than three particles and especially exclusive cross sections in TDDFT without spurious cross-channel correlations remain conceptually unresolved; modern reviews still list these as open problems. Therefore the overall program is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Pair Correlations and the Time-Dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov Method in the Theory of Nuclear Structure
status_evidence.snippet: Time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov method has made a strong impact on the development of modern nuclear theory.
status_evidence.claim: TDHFB equations for pair-correlated dynamics have been formulated and partially implemented.

status_evidence.title: 3D solution of Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov equations for drip-line nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: 3D HFB solutions with proper continuum treatment for drip-line nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Static HFB with correct asymptotics for drip-line nuclei has been achieved, providing the basis for time-dependent extensions.

status_evidence.title: Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov theory for odd-mass nuclei with a time-odd constraint and application to deformed halo nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Application of HFB to deformed halo (drip-line) nuclei with continuum and pairing.
status_evidence.claim: Pairing-plus-continuum treatments for weakly bound nuclei continue to be an active, only partially resolved area.
